_schema_notes.coverage: Authoritative schema for all DID formats — DD Form 1664 (pre-2014) and free-text (post-2014 MIL-STD-963C)
_schema_notes.did_format: Set to 'dd_form_1664' or 'free_text'. Determines which fields are expected to be populated.
_schema_notes.963c_compliant: True if the DID was prepared under MIL-STD-963C (2014 or later). False for older DIDs.
_schema_notes.reserved_fields: Fields marked RESERVED are present in one format but not the other. Always include them — set to empty string or empty array when not applicable.
_schema_notes.preparation_instructions: Official MIL-STD-963C name for what was previously called 'requirements'. Contains the numbered sections of the DID. All section numbers are normalized to strictly numeric dot-notation (1, 1.1, 1.1.1). Letter-based source numbering (2.a, 3.1.b) is converted to numeric equivalents (2.1, 3.1.2).
_schema_notes.asterisk: True if the requirement number is followed by * in the source document (conditional requirement).

title: Hazard Tracking System (HTS) Data
summary: Specifies the format and content for Hazard Tracking System (HTS) Data used to document and track hazard tracking and Software Level of Rigor information required by MIL-STD-882E(C1).
use_relationship:
The Hazard Tracking System (HTS) Data will be used to document and track essential information from contractors for accomplishing the tracking system requirements of MIL-STD-882E(C1). This data includes the closed loop hazard tracking requirements in MIL-STD-882E(C1) paragraph 4.3.1.d and Task 106 as well as the Software Level of Rigor (LOR) Data requirements of paragraph 4.4.3.

This Data Item Description (DID) contains the format, content, and intended use information for the data deliverable resulting from the work tasks described in MIL-STD-882E(C1). This applies to all developmental and sustaining engineering activities for the Department of Defense (DoD) systems, equipment, and facilities. This DID also contains additional data elements required when MIL-STD-882E(C1) Detailed Requirements Tasks are applied to the contract.

(Copies of this document are available online at https://quicksearch.dla.mil.)

This DID supersedes DI-SAFT-82085

references.label: Copies of this document are available online

distribution_statement: DISTRIBUTION STATEMENT A: Approved for public release; distribution is unlimited.

preparation_instructions.title: Reference documents
preparation_instructions.content: The applicable issue of the documents cited herein, including their approval dates and dates of any applicable amendments, notices, and revisions, shall be as specified in the contract.

preparation_instructions.title: Format
preparation_instructions.content: The HTS database shall be in a format compatible with government office capabilities. Data shall be delivered in one of these formats; (e.g., software tools/applications such as spreadsheets or databases).

preparation_instructions.title: Content
preparation_instructions.content: The HTS shall contain the following information:

children.title: Unique Hazard Identifier
children.content: Identifier used for positive Closed-Loop Hazard Tracking.

children.title: System/Subsystem Description
children.content: Information needed to describe the system or subsystem. Typical Topics Include:

children.title: System/subsystem interfaces
children.content: System/subsystem interfaces of interest to included interfaces between subsystems, between hardware and software, between different units of software, with the environment, with the human, and to include Architectural/Facility Enterprises.

children.title: Hardware
children.content: Information needed to properly characterize hardware being cited, if applicable. Typical Topics Include:

children.title: Specific Component Configuration(s) and related Configuration History
Manufacturing Details (forging, milling, casting, additive manufacturing, etc.)
Software
children.content: Information needed to properly characterize software being cited, if applicable. Typical Topics Include:

children.title: The program's definition of what a Unit
children.content: The program's definition of what a Unit of Software is (e.g. Computer Software Configuration Item (CSCI), Computer Software Component (CSC), Computer Software Unit (CSU); this definition is to be used in all documentation required by this DID.

children.title: Unit(s) of software associated with the hazard
Additional clarification of where within the unit of software relates to the hazard
Human (Consider/Use occupational health data)
children.content: Information needed to describe how the human is involved in a hazard, if applicable. Typical Topics Include:

children.title: Exposure to physical, chemical, radiological, biological hazardous conditions
Environment
children.content: (Consider/Use environmental data) Information needed to describe how undesired environment effects (e.g. wind, precipitation, light, etc.) are involved in a hazard, if applicable.

children.title: Hazard Description
children.content: Information needed to sufficiently describe the hazard. Typical Topics Include:

children.title: Modes of operation of interest (normal, emergency, maintenance, text, disposal, etc.)
Environmental interfaces (vibration, heat, exposure to corrosive substances, etc.)
Hazard effects involving hardware, software, human, environmental
Safety Relationship to Requirements
children.content: Those requirements with a relationship to safety. This shall include citations for a system's safety requirement or requirements associated with hazard controls.

children.title: Risk Assessment
children.content: Details needed to properly document a hazard. Typical Topics Include:

children.title: Assertions and assumptions behind Severity (Per MIL-STD-882E(C1) Table I)
Assertions and assumptions behind Probability (Per MIL-STD-882E(C1) Table II)
children.content: include all math in the derivation of quantitative probabilities

children.title: Identify all unknown data associated with the hazard
Resultant Risk (Per MIL-STD-882E(C1) Table III) for "Initial Risk", "Risk As of Today", "Target Risk", and/or "Event Risk" (aka Test Event)
Unique conditions during a special event
Hazard Controls
children.content: Document the hazard controls associated with a hazard. Typical Topics Include:

children.title: An explanation of each selected hazard control
An association with the selected hazard controls and the System Safety Order of Precedence
Reducing Probability (aka Mitigation) or Severity (aka Amelioration)
Projected amount of "risk" bought back (e.g. the amount of risk reduction as the result of incorporating hazard controls)
Schedule for each control to be installed throughout fleet
Verification control implemented into design (verifications of risk reduction)
Validation control achieving desired hazard intervention
Hazard Status
children.content: Description of the hazard status. Typical Topics Include:

children.title: Formal acceptance by the Risk Acceptance Authority
Related Hazards
children.content: Referenced to other related hazards.

children.title: Other
children.content: Related anomalies, incidents, or mishaps.

children.title: Such citations shall not cite Limited Use Mishap Data
Any other items (i.e., studies, analyses, test data, notes or similar data) generated in the performance of the contract with respect to the HTS
Software LOR Data
children.content: This data is generated as a result of MIL-STD-882E(C1) paragraph 4.4.

children.title: Unit of Software
children.content: Information needed to properly characterize software being cited. The program's definition of what a Unit of Software is (e.g. CSCI, CSC, CSU); this definition is to be used in all documentation required by this DID.

children.title: SwCI/LOR Determination
children.content: The rationale supporting how the Software Criticality Index (SwCI)/LOR was derived for each Unit of Software. Typical Discussion Includes

children.title: For each unit of software, the Software Control Category
children.content: For each unit of software, the Software Control Category (SCC; MIL-STD-882E(C1) Table IV) and supporting rationale for determining applicable SCC.

children.title: For each unit of software, the rationale behind determining
children.content: For each unit of software, the rationale behind determining worst potential Severity (MIL-STD-882E(C1) Table I) for the software unit. Several hazards may involve the same unit of software, the most severe Severity is used.

children.title: MIL-STD-882E(C1) Table V Results for the software unit's SwCI and tier of LOR
Describe each LOR Activity for each LOR Tier (corresponding to SwCI Tier)
Provide LOR artifacts correlated to each LOR activity for each Unit of Software
Define the timeline when MIL-STD-882E(C1) Table VI questions
children.content: Define the timeline when MIL-STD-882E(C1) Table VI questions are to be asked. (e.g. prior to Preliminary Design Review - PDR; prior to Critical Design Review - CDR; prior to formal testing; prior to fielding, periodically during sustainment).

children.title: For each Unit of Software, provide status of
children.content: For each Unit of Software, provide status of MIL-STD-882E(C1) Table VI question for each LOR Activity

children.title: Annotate what is left to be defined
Annotate Government Program Management (PM) decision to expend
children.content: Annotate Government Program Management (PM) decision to expend additional resources to define LOR activity or obtain Risk Acceptance Authority's formal acceptance for the unspecified LOR Tier. If unavailable, highlight the need for a decision to be made.

children.title: For each incomplete (e.g. non-compliant) LOR activity
Annotate specifically what is incomplete with the LOR criteria
Annotate Government PM decision to expend additional
children.content: Annotate Government PM decision to expend additional resources to define LOR activity or obtain Risk Acceptance Authority's formal acceptance for the incomplete LOR activity. If unavailable, highlight the need for a decision to be made.
